subject: ClearHealth usage reconciliation + settlement pathway
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearhealth.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@clearhealth.io
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: usage reconciliation request — Q2 spike

Hi Grace / Ben,

Hope you’re both well. We completed our internal monthly review and saw an unexpected spike in inference hours for July — roughly 480k additional token-hours billed outside our committed capacity. Can you help clarify how that usage is being billed and what options we have to reconcile? Our procurement lead (cc’d) needs a short path to close this out before our month-end accounts.

Attached I’ve included the usage export (high level) and a quick note on how our finance team would prefer to see a one-time top-up vs amortized charge. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Integrations
ClearHealth

---
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearhealth.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@clearhealth.io
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: usage reconciliation request — Q2 spike

Alex — thanks for the note and the export. We reviewed the rows and it looks like a combination of a traffic surge and a model change that increased average token length for a small set of endpoints. Ben is pulling the exact per-route charge breakdown.

To move quickly and keep your month-end tidy, here’s a proposed pathway:

- Option A (recommended): One-time top-up invoice for the overage (line-itemized by route). We can apply a 10% settlement credit if paid within 30 days.
- Option B: Amortize over the next 3 invoices (no credit) and lock-in a 5% discounted unit rate for two quarters as a gesture for the spike.
- Documentation: We’ll attach the per-route CSV and draft invoice for approval.

Next steps I propose: Ben will send the draft invoice + line items today. Alex / procurement to confirm preferred path (A or B) and provide PO details if going with Option A.

If you prefer, we can also do a partial credit now and reconcile the remainder.

Best,
Grace O
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_settlement_template_v1.pdf (draft invoice template, PDF stub)

---
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearhealth.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@clearhealth.io
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: usage reconciliation request — Q2 spike

Grace — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement prefers Option A (one-time top-up) but requests the charge be split into two line items: (1) pure overage (hours x rate) and (2) a one-time stabilization fee for the model rollout that caused the spike. Can you itemize those separately?

I attached the usage export we ran locally (clearhealth_usage_report_Q2.csv) — the spike maps to endpoints /v1/patient-summary and /v1/smart-fill between July 12–17. If you can include per-endpoint token counts and the effective unit price, procurement can generate the PO same day.

Also, can Redwood confirm the month the model change went live so we have the timeline for our auditor?

Thanks — Alex

Attachment: clearhealth_usage_report_Q2.csv (CSV stub)

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearhealth.io>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@clearhealth.io
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: usage reconciliation request — Q2 spike

Alex — thanks for the details. We dug into the billing logs and produced the attached line-item invoice draft (see redwood_settlement_draft_v1.pdf). Summary below: 

- Overage (token-hours): $42,750 (per-endpoint breakdown in PDF)
- Stabilization fee (one-time): $5,000
- Subtotal: $47,750
- Early-payment settlement credit (10% applied if paid within 30 days): -$4,775
- Total (if Option A + early payment): $42,975

We also confirmed the model variant causing higher token-length rolled live on 2026-07-11 (release tag: prod/v2.14). I’ve added that note to the invoice for audit purposes.

DocuSign and invoice links: https://www.docusign.com/clearhealth-settlement-CH-DL-2026-09 (draft).

If procurement confirms PO number and chooses Option A, we’ll finalize and send a DocuSign-ready invoice. If they prefer amortization, I can produce a three-month amortization schedule.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_settlement_draft_v1.pdf (PDF stub)

---
From: Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@clearhealth.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearhealth.io>, procurement@clearhealth.io, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: usage reconciliation request — Q2 spike

Grace / Ben — thanks for the clear options and the audit note. ClearHealth will proceed with Option A. Procurement will issue PO CH-PO-2026-339 by end of day tomorrow to cover the total after the early-payment credit ($42,975). Two asks before we close:

1) Please embed the prod/v2.14 release tag and the per-endpoint token counts on the final invoice PDF (for our internal audit).
2) We need the DocuSign envelope to be sent to procurement@clearhealth.io and finance@clearhealth.io; please mark Grace as the primary contact on the invoice.

Once we have the PO number we’ll sign the DocuSign and wire. Appreciate the 10% early-payment credit — that made the decision straightforward.

Regards,
Dana Schultz
SVP, Finance — ClearHealth

-----
Grace O
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
redwood.ai
